ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (transposing EU Directives 2015/849 and 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 August 2019 on the RBE; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; AML/CFT obligations of the Luxembourg notariat pursuant to the Law of 9 December 1976 on notaries, as amended; and the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as modified by the Law of 23 July 2016 creating the SCSp regime).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized true-certified copies of the passport and residence card of each beneficial owner and of the proposed general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the individual's country of residence (e.g., PRC notary for Chinese principals)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or consular legalization for non-Apostille states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of the corporate general partner, if any (e.g., a Luxembourg SOPARFI or foreign holding entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) or the competent corporate registry of the general partner's home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization if the issuer is in a non-Apostille jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney appointing the Luxembourg incorporation counsel and registered-agent service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the appointing partners' jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization at the competent consulate in Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of Wealth and Source of Funds statement with supporting bank reference letter and account statements covering the last 12 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Deposit-taking bank and notary public of the client's jurisdiction; Luxembourg notarial certification for EU-issued statements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for bank-issued statements from non-EU states; Luxembourg notarial certification for EU statements

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Beneficial Owner declaration (RBE form) executed by each partner and the SCSp's proposed general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Partners and general partner, countersigned by the Luxembourg notary or attorney-at-law
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Luxembourg notarial signature certificate (no apostille required for domestic Luxembourg acts)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and screening of all UBOs, the general partner, and source-of-funds providers against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN List, and Luxembourg FIU domestic warnings, in accordance with the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be identified using a risk-based approach, with senior-management approval for high-risk relationships, enhanced ongoing monitoring, and documentary retention for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic portal (www.lbr.lu); user support via Guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filings are made in French or German; the selected name may be in Luxembourgish, French, German, or any language written in Latin script. Non-Latin names must be transliterated into Latin characters in the partnership agreement and RCS filing. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must be preceded or followed by the legal-form suffix 'SCSp' or the full French denomination 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'. No ministerial authorization is required for ordinary names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: chambre de commerce / chamber of commerce
Luxembourg Stock Exchange / Bourse de Luxembourg
SA / SARL / SE / SCA / SCS (misleading legal-form tokens)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RCS rejection, the applicant files a written request for reconsideration with the RCS Registrar within 15 days of the rejection notice, attaching a fresh name-clearance search and a memorandum on distinctiveness. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may bring judicial proceedings before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within 40 days of the final administrative decision. The court may order the RCS to register the name; statutory costs and attorney fees are recoverable upon success. Concurrently, the applicant may re-submit and reserve an alternative name without prejudice under a new 30-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally acceptable pre-incorporation: an RCS-recognized third-party registered-office provider may be designated before the partnership premises are finalized; however, an ISIC 3091 electric cargo bike manufacturer must establish a physical production or assembly facility and the general partner must demonstrate real decision-making, staff, and economic substance in Luxembourg. Purely virtual arrangements expose the SCSp to scrutiny under the Luxembourg GAAR and ATAD-transposing rules, as well as to FIU and tax-substance challenges.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% annualized probability for this Low_Risk_Standard manufacturing tier; unannounced on-site controls by Luxembourg tax or VAT authorities are not routine but increase to approximately 20% if the registered office is exclusively virtual, RBE data is inconsistent, or adverse-media or sanctions alerts are triggered.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate legal consultation and drafting of the SCSp partnership agreement (English/French) including UBO structure analysis
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Attorney-at-law registered with the Luxembourg Bar

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (tarif réglementé) and prevailing market benchmark
Statutory tariff of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation announcement in the official electronic compendium (RESA)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner initial declaration filing with the RBE
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (Luxembourg Ministry of Justice)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC notary public and PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Consular Department)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of the PRC (notarization fee + MFA apostille fee + courier)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address and mail-forwarding service, first 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RCS-licensed corporate and registered-agent service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SCSp registered-office packages

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Consolidated Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, including the special limited partnership regime for the Société en Commandite Spéciale introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; supplemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the amended Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to craft, industrial and commercial professions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - operator of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (Statuts) accompanied by the standardised RCS registration data form (Formulaire D) submitted through the electronic e-RCS portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed on an SCSp; contributions are freely determined by the partners in the articles of association and may be made in cash or in kind. No escrow account is legally required. Contributions must be credited to the SCSp's bank account and confirmed by a capital-receipt certificate before registration with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby approve the partnership interests in the Société en Commandite Spéciale as set forth in the draft articles of association, and confirm the respective capital contributions to be made by each general and limited partner. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the SCSp be established at the address indicated in the articles, in Luxembourg, effective upon incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the general partner is hereby appointed Manager (Gérant) of the SCSp, with full power to manage, represent, and bind the partnership. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Manager is authorized to complete all filings with the Luxembourg Business Registers and to take all necessary steps for registration and publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - e-RCS name search and certificate desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the proposed legal name against the RCS database and obtain a non-registration attestation from LBR. Verify that the name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered entity and that no protected public-order term is used. Retain the attestation in the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Proposed legal name as set out in the draft statuts
Identification documents of each general and limited partner
Ultimate beneficial owner confirmation where requested by LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of identity or similarity, submit three alternate names through the e-RCS counter. LBR processes the refusal notice within one business day and re-filing of an acceptable name does not attract an additional search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and legalization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires) or authenticated private signing followed by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts incorporating the SCSp's corporate purpose of design, assembly, and distribution of electric cargo bicycles, management clauses, contribution terms, and Luxembourg governing law. Execute by notarial deed or by private deed with certified signatures and present the original to the AEDT for payment of the fixed registration duty.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of passports or national identity cards of all partners
Corporate registry extract and board resolution for any corporate general partner
Notarized or certified power of attorney for signatories
Statutory declaration of eligibility where non-resident partners are concerned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the AEDT queries a formal defect, file a corrective deed (acte rectificatif) signed in the same manner. Corrections do not attract proportional registration duty where the subscribed capital and the identity of the partners remain unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and capital contribution certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Euro-denominated bank account in the name of the SCSp being formed, deposit the agreed initial contributions, and request a capital-receipt certificate addressed to the future RCS file. The certificate is issued once funds are finally settled and unencumbered.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association or evidence of incorporation intent
Identification and tax residence proof of each beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises additional compliance queries, provide a corporate structure chart and certified passport copies. If clearance exceeds five business days, open the account at an alternative Luxembourg bank and formally release the first bank from any reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the Register of Commerce and Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - e-RCS filing counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Authenticate on the e-RCS portal, complete Formulaire D containing entity data, upload the executed statuts, the capital-receipt certificate, the Manager's letter of acceptance, and the RCS fee payment. Monitor the issuance of the official RCS registration extract and record the registration number.
required_dossiers: Letter of acceptance and specimen signatures of the Manager
Proof of payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for supplementary information (demande de complément), respond within one month through a corrective e-RCS filing. An unanswered application is deemed withdrawn, but a complete resubmission within five business days preserves the original priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory publication in the official electronic journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RESA publication section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the RCS registration extract, the registration data is automatically transmitted to the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA). Verify the published notice, confirm the publication date, and obtain a certified copy of the notice for the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Payment confirmation of the publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed beyond the service standard, submit a written expedite request to LBR. Any typographical error in the RESA notice is remedied by filing a rectification notice with effect from the date of the original publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration commercial, tax, and social security activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Guichet unique des autorisations; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the business establishment authorization reflecting the manufacturing scope, register the SCSp for Luxembourg VAT at the AEDT, register as an employer at the CCSS, and file the beneficial owner declaration in the Register of Beneficial Owners. Arrange accounting and economic substance records appropriate to an operational manufacturing entity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment authorization is queried, answer the technical questionnaire within fifteen days. VAT registration may be antedated to the incorporation date on demonstration of good faith, and the CCSS accepts a corrected payroll declaration without penalty when filed within the legal tolerance period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des classes moyennes, acting through the Guichet unique des autorisations d'établissement (MyGuichet.lu)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement pour l'exercice d'une activité industrielle - manufacture and assembly of electric cargo bicycles and step-through scooters

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement - Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Classified establishment, 2nd class, under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 relating to classified establishments (commodo/incommodo). A full EIA report under the amended Law of 15 May 2018 is not triggered unless the plant's coating lines consume 150 tonnes or more of organic solvents per year or on-site hazardous waste storage, including lithium-ion batteries, exceeds 100 tonnes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater must meet the discharge limits of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 8 March 2017 on discharges into surface water, including pH 6-9, COD not exceeding 125 mg/L, BOD5 not exceeding 25 mg/L, and suspended solids not exceeding 35 mg/L. Controlled coating and painting operations must comply with Directive 2010/75/EU, with stack VOC emissions limited to 50 mg C/Nm3 and a solvent management plan. Lithium-ion battery waste must be consigned under hazardous waste code 16 06 05, with full waste acceptance documentation and take-back obligations under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Administration des services de secours (CGDIS) covering evacuation routes and extinguishing systems; structural load inspection certificate from an approved engineer for storage mezzanines and battery storage areas; occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) addressing electrical safety, ventilation, noise exposure, and segregated storage of lithium batteries.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue is bifurcated: the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) administers direct corporate and personal income tax, while the Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) administers VAT, registration duties, and excise; the unified e-government portal is MyGuichet.lu, with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) handling entity registration and filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SCSp partnership agreement before a Luxembourg notary and file for registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) to obtain the RCS registration number and national identification number. Step 2: Submit the business commencement declaration (formule 640) to the AEDT within 15 days of commencing taxable activity; a non-resident or non-established partnership must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative if no fixed establishment exists. Step 3: Receive the VAT identification number in the format LU followed by eight digits. Step 4: Enroll with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for social security if personnel are employed. Step 5: Foreign partners must supply certified constitutional documents, a Luxembourg registered office address, and a local authorized manager (gérant) to complete direct-tax registration; because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, individual partners are assessed directly by the ACD on their allocable share of income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. An SCSp is fiscally transparent by default but is statutorily re-characterized as a taxable corporate entity under the hybrid-mismatch override at Article 5bis K of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) to the extent a partner is not subject to net-basis taxation in Luxembourg, thereby neutralizing hybrid entity mismatches under ATAD. VAT-specific elections include: waiver of the small-business exemption under Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, formation of a VAT group as a single taxable person under Article 60 of the VAT Law, and application of the reverse-charge mechanism for intra-Community acquisitions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover (small-business exemption threshold under Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law); mandatory VAT registration is required absent any turnover threshold for imports, intra-EU acquisitions, distance sales, and reverse-charge transactions; the threshold is measured on a rolling calendar-year basis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory business-to-government (B2G) e-invoicing via the Peppol eDelivery Network has been in force since 2021; there is no general mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping for business-to-business invoices in the e-bike manufacturing sector; VAT SAF-T (Standard Audit File for Tax) files must be transmitted electronically to the AEDT by prescribed taxpayers; Intrastat and VIES recapitulative statements must be filed electronically through MyGuichet; invoices must comply with EU Directive 2014/55/EU syntax and semantic standards.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of electric cargo e-bikes to destinations outside the European Union are exempt with credit for input VAT (effective 0% rate) under Article 55 of the Luxembourg VAT Law provided the goods physically leave the EU customs territory and transport is evidenced; intra-Community dispatches to a VAT-registered customer are zero-rated when the customer's valid VIES VAT identification number is recorded; offshore B2B services benefit from zero-rating under the general place-of-supply reverse-charge rule pursuant to Article 58 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; supporting documentation must be retained for at least 10 years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A / SAD single administrative document) lodged electronically through the Luxembourg customs clearance system (GUS/ECS)
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) or CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT transfer confirmation demonstrating repatriation of export sale proceeds
Commercial invoice and executed sale contract with Incoterms 2020 allocation of risk and transport cost
Proof of transport (carrier track-and-trace report or customs-stamped logistics documentation)
Intrastat dispatch return or VIES recapitulative statement in respect of intra-EU zero-rated supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or improperly substantiated export zero-rating claims trigger retrospective VAT assessments under the standard 5-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud; statutory late-interest accrues from the original due date; the AEDT may impose administrative fines of up to EUR 250,000 pursuant to Article 131 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, together with a 10% surcharge on the VAT due; willful tax fraud is a criminal offense under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung) punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years; exporters of high-risk goods face enhanced audit scrutiny and potential clawback of previously recovered input VAT credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem, in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for prudential supervision and the European Central Bank for monetary and foreign-exchange policy; Luxembourg applies no national foreign-exchange control authority separate from the Eurosystem.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account items under Articles 63-65 TFEU; there are zero residual exchange controls for euro-denominated flows or cross-border profit remittances. An SCSp tax-transparent entity faces no FX licence or convertibility restriction on dividend, interest, or liquidation distributions; only informational reporting applies (BCL balance-of-payments statistics, FATCA/CRS self-certification).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law imposes no statutory timeline, minimum conversion ratio, or surrender obligation on export receipts; exporters may retain USD, CNY, GBP, or EUR balances freely in operational accounts. The only applicable duties are periodic balance-of-payments statistical declarations to the BCL and standard AML/CFT transaction reporting under the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account And Inbound Investment Wallet

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: FEASIBILITY RATING: MEDIUM-HIGH for low-value disbursements, LOW for core treasury. Luxembourg-authorised EMIs under PSD2 may hold payment accounts, but a manufacturing SCSp requires a CSSF-licensed credit institution to access SWIFT MT100/MT700 clearing, documentary-credit issuance, trade-finance limits, and multi-currency nostro rails. Offshore digital EMIs cannot hold capital-escrow structures or issue commercial LCs; the recommended architecture is a Luxembourg core banking relationship augmented by one EMI payment gateway for small operational spend.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The SCSp is not a separate legal person; accounts are opened in the partnership name through the General Partner. Physical interview of the General Partner's authorised manager and principal UBOs at the bank's Luxembourg premises remains the prevailing market standard for non-EEA ownership. Remote video onboarding is available under CSSF implementation of EBA Guidelines EBA/GL/2022/15 only when the bank operates a compliant digital-identification system, and it is usually supplemented by a notarised, apostilled power of attorney and a Luxembourg registered-agent confirmation. In practice, at least one in-person or CSSF-registered correspondent KYC session is required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque SCSp ownership: bearer or nominee limited-partner interests conceal ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed partnership agreement with full LP interest schedule; General Partner certificate identifying all UBOs; Luxembourg RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) extract confirming post-closing registration; nominee/trust arrangement declarations under Article 6 of the AML Law of 12 November 2004, as amended; consolidated corporate ownership chart; passports and proof of address of each UBO and authorised signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound capital injection from a non-EU parent flagged as unsubstantiated source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Latest three-year audited financial statements of the contributing investor; corporate resolutions approving the capital call and equity injection; investor bank reference letter; underlying OEM supply or licensing contract substantiating commercial rationale; funds-flow schedule; signed Source of Wealth and Source of Funds statements; negative-match sanctions screening confirmation under EU Regulation 269/2014 and CSSF guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparency and substance mismatch: SCSp perceived as a shell because Luxembourg payroll and premises are minimal relative to manufacturing turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance dossier comprising Luxembourg registered-office or coordination-suite lease; payroll and social-security filings with Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale; commercial insurance; General Partner and board meeting minutes evidencing real decision-making; intercompany transfer-pricing documentation for OEM royalties and component sales; FATCA/CRS tax self-certifications of all UBOs; Certificate of Good Standing of the General Partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering indicators: over-invoicing, duplicate invoicing, or quality/quantity mismatches on electric cargo-bike component imports from Asia.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UCP 600-compliant documentation set: commercial invoices with HS codes and unit economics; packing lists; bills of lading or airway bills; certificates of origin; independent pre-shipment inspection certificates; customs entry declarations (ECS/ITF); insurance certificates; matching SWIFT MT103 payment records; counterparty KYC and negative-media/sanctions screening outcome.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing for SCSp capital calls and shareholder loans: SWIFT MT103 from the parent/investor with BCL balance-of-payments purpose code 'D' (direct investment) or 'EQUI' for equity and 'LOAN' for shareholder debt, accompanied by a capital-call notice, partner resolutions, executed loan agreement at arm's-length interest, and the bank's AML Source-of-Funds form. EEA-origin euro injections clear via SEPA Credit Transfer or TARGET2 Immediate for same-day value; non-EEA euro wires arrive via correspondent TARGET2 ties. Large contributions above EUR 50,000 trigger pre-transaction compliance clearance; no BCL approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier payments, MT700/MT710 for documentary import/export letters of credit under UCP 600, and MT760 for standby credits under ISP98. Euro leg clears through TARGET2 and Instant SEPA; USD leg through CHIPS/Fedwire; CNY through the Luxembourg Renminbi clearing facility operated by ICBC Europe S.A. All outbound flows are automatically screened against EU sanctions, restrictive measures, and dual-use goods controls under EU Regulation 2021/821.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC deliverable EUR/CNH foreign-exchange forwards with tenors of 1 to 24 months subject to approved credit lines
EUR/USD and EUR/GBP outright forwards and rolling forward contracts
FX swaps (spot against forward) for USD/EUR/CNH liquidity optimisation
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing onshore CNY, INR, or BRL for component-sourcing exposures
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) converting fixed-rate shareholder loans into floating or matched-currency obligations
Plain-vanilla FX options and participating forwards; all instruments subject to EMIR clearing/reporting, MiFID-II suitability, and CSSF collateralisation rules

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined for Luxembourg City: corporate income tax 17% + solidarity surcharge 0.70% (7% of CIT) + municipal business tax 6.75% (commune rate; ranges up to 11.20% outside Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent: no corporate income tax at the entity level; profits and gains are allocated to partners and taxed in their hands. Preferential deductions at partner level: 100% participation exemption for qualifying substantial shareholdings (holding >= 10% or acquisition price >= EUR 6,000,000, continuously held 12 months); 80% exemption for net qualifying IP income under the Luxembourg IP box (effective rate approx. 5%); EUR 17,500 annual exemption base for municipal business tax; no net wealth tax levied on the transparent partnership itself. No statutory tax holiday applies to the electric cargo bike manufacturing activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 470 (Declaration for fiscally transparent partnerships, sociétés de personnes), filed electronically via the Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD) e-Filing portal on MyGuichet.lu with LuxTrust authentication; the return is an allocative/informational return and does not itself compute entity-level CIT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year is the calendar year unless otherwise approved. Paper-filed returns are due by 31 March of the year following the fiscal year (N+1); electronic filing through the ACD portal automatically extends the deadline to 31 December of year N+1. Late-filed returns trigger reminder procedures and estimated assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the SCSp, RCS Luxembourg registration number, registered office address, and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp must maintain a Luxembourg registered office and appoint a Luxembourg-based authorised representative; attach the RCS extract showing the registered address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates; accounting framework applied (Lux GAAP or IFRS); balance sheet date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should align the SCSp fiscal year to the calendar year for efficient reporting; a first period may be shorter than 12 months if the partnership was formed mid-year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 11/12 (Résultat global / Total profit or loss)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total net profit or loss of the partnership for the fiscal year before allocation, as per the statutory accounts, including all manufacturing, trading, and financial income of the electric cargo bike OEM activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full Luxembourg-source and foreign-source income attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment; attach a tax reconciliation schedule showing depreciation, inventory adjustments, and any disallowed expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For each partner: name, country of residence, profit-sharing percentage, allocated income or loss amount, and the DTA article on which the partner relies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each non-resident partner must hold a valid certificate of tax residence (TRC) from its state of residence; if the partner is a company, attach a UBO declaration and evidence of beneficial ownership. Allocation shares must follow the partnership agreement and not the nominal capital distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 15 (ICC add-backs / Municipal business tax base)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back adjustments to the trade tax base: 50% of interest paid to related parties (non-bank) and 25% of royalties paid to related parties; net operating losses used.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners with no Luxembourg permanent establishment are generally not subject to Luxembourg municipal business tax on their allocable share; the SCSp itself remains the ICC taxpayer for the commercial activity carried on in Luxembourg and must file Form 7.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 470: administrative scale fines normally between EUR 120 and EUR 2,500 per return; late payment interest on assessed taxes accrues monthly at 0.8% of the amount due; failure to file after formal notice triggers estimated assessments, a possible 10% increase of the assessed tax base, and criminal prosecution for deliberate non-filing with fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years in aggravated fraud cases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 7 (Municipal Business Tax / Impôt commercial communal, ICC) filed with the same ACD e-Filing portal via MyGuichet.lu; the SCSp is the ICC taxpayer for its commercial manufacturing activity in Luxembourg.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same cycle as Form 470: due 31 March of year N+1 in paper, automatically extended to 31 December N+1 when filed electronically; prepayments of ICC are due quarterly on 10 February, 10 May, 10 August, and 10 November based on the prior year's base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit for the fiscal year, before distribution, adjusted by add-backs (50% related-party interest, 25% related-party royalties) and reliefs (EUR 17,500 basic allowance, participation exemption share).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, only the profit allocable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment is included; if the SCSp merely holds participations and does not trade, no ICC is due and a nil return should still be filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal multiplier applied by the commune of the registered seat or PE; Luxembourg City rate is 6.75% for 2024/2025.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact commune and verify the applicable rate with the communal tax authority; manufacturing inventory located at a warehouse may create a PE in another commune, triggering allocation of the ICC base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reference line declaring whether the entity is subject to net wealth tax; the transparent SCSp is not a taxpayer of net wealth tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners may need to report their allocable share of Luxembourg PE assets in their own net wealth tax filings in their residence country; no Luxembourg net wealth tax applies to the partnership itself.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 7 or under-declared ICC carries the same scale fines as Form 470 (EUR 120 to EUR 2,500 per return) plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.8%; repeated non-compliance leads to estimated assessment and a 10% penalty uplift; deliberate under-declaration for ICC constitutes tax fraud with criminal fines up to EUR 250,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory domestic dividend withholding tax is 15% (LIR Art. 101) for distributions by Luxembourg companies. For the SCSp specifically, profit allocations and capital distributions to partners are not dividends: the fiscally transparent partnership does not levy withholding tax at the entity level, and no WHT is applied on allocations of manufacturing or trading profits to either resident or non-resident partners. Where the SCSp receives dividends from an operating subsidiary, that subsidiary applies the 15% WHT at source, subject to full exemption under the Luxembourg participation exemption and to 0% under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief on any Luxembourg-source dividends, interest, or royalties flowing in the structure, the following protocol applies: (1) the beneficial owner (partner or shareholder) obtains a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from its state of residence issued within the previous 12 months; (2) the payer or the SCSp's general partner submits the TRC along with a completed DTA relief application and UBO declaration to the Luxembourg ACD, either through the MyGuichet.lu e-platform or in writing to the competent bureau d'imposition; (3) for EU/EEA TRCs no legalisation or apostille is required; for non-EU states an apostille may be requested; (4) the payer applies the reduced DTA rate at source (exonération ou réduction à la source) once the relief has been admitted, or the foreign recipient claims a refund within the five-year statutory limitation period by filing the refund application with the ACD refund service; (5) the SCSp must demonstrate that the partner is the ultimate beneficial owner and that the income is not routed through a conduit lacking substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: no statutory Luxembourg withholding tax applies to ordinary arm's length interest paid by a Luxembourg payer to non-residents; DTA rates for source-state taxation of interest range from 0% to 15%, with most Luxembourg treaties applying 5-10% and several at 0% when the recipient is the beneficial owner. Royalties: Luxembourg does not impose a domestic withholding tax on royalties paid out by a Luxembourg payer under current domestic law; under treaties, source-state WHT on patent, know-how, and commercial royalties is usually 0% (e.g., Luxembourg-United States, Luxembourg-Germany at 5%) subject to beneficial ownership, and to the OECD anti-fragmentation and substance rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg TP documentation must be maintained where the annual aggregate value of controlled transactions with related parties exceeds EUR 1,000,000 for goods or services; EUR 300,000 for financial transactions (loans, guarantees, cash pooling); and EUR 100,000 for other transactions (including IP and management fees). A Master File is additionally required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 50,000,000. The transparent SCSp is subject to these rules where it carries on a commercial activity (e.g., intra-group procurement of components, licensing of design IP or intercompany financing for the e-bike manufacturing operation).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not codify a standalone Economic Substance Regulation statute, but economic substance is legally enforced through the domestic general anti-abuse rule (Steueranpassungsgesetz / Abus de droit doctrine), the ATAD general anti-abuse and interest limitation rules, and the administrative practice requiring a real Luxembourg presence for transparent vehicles. The SCSp must be managed in Luxembourg: general partner decision-making, local registered office, local bank accounts, and genuine commercial or holding activity commensurate with its income. Without substance, the tax authorities may recharacterise the SCSp as a fully taxable opaque entity, deny DTA and EU Directive benefits, retroactively reassess up to ten years, and apply a 10% abuse-related uplift. For the electric cargo bike OEM activity, the manufacturing intellectual property, purchase orders, inventory management and commercial risk must be substantiated in Luxembourg with economic functions and personnel.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion (fiscal fraud and wilful omission)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to declare Luxembourg-source allocable profits of the SCSp; submission of falsified invoices, overstated inventory or fictitious manufacturing costs; concealment of the true identities of non-resident partners; omission of allocable income to Luxembourg corporate or individual partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 (and up to double the evaded tax in aggravated cases); imprisonment up to 5 years; administrative 100% malevolent omission surcharge on the evaded tax; monthly late-payment interest at 0.8%; disallowance of loss carryforwards; seizure of assets through attachment orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner (commandité) has unlimited joint and several liability for the debts of the SCSp. Managers and directors of a corporate general partner are personally liable for civil restitution of the evaded amounts; criminal courts may impose travel bans, entry restrictions, seizure of bank accounts, asset freezes, and imprisonment. Limited partners who participate in day-to-day management lose their limited liability shield and become jointly liable with the general partner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / absence of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a letterbox entity: no staff, no physical office or manufacturing warehouse in Luxembourg, no local control over procurement or sales; routing of passive dividends, interest or IP royalties through the partnership without any real economic activity; use of the transparent status solely to obtain tax treaty benefits for non-resident partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the SCSp as a fully taxable Luxembourg resident company; assessment to 24.94% combined CIT and municipal business tax plus net wealth tax exposure; denial of treaty benefits and Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief; retroactive reassessment over 10 years; 10% abuse-of-law uplift on the taxable base; fines up to EUR 250,000 for tax fraud where the sham is intentional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner are jointly liable for the reassessed taxes and penalties where insolvency follows the recharacterisation; the corporate veil is pierced in fraud cases, leading to personal civil liability, freezing orders, travel restrictions and criminal prosecution of the directing minds. Non-resident shareholders who knowingly structure a sham can be co-prosecuted as accomplices.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation failure and non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a Local File / Master File once the statutory thresholds are exceeded; pricing of intra-group component sales, management fees, technology royalties, or shareholder loans at rates departing from arm's length; undocumented loans with zero interest or unilateral cost allocations without a TP study; late or zero filing of the TP documentation upon ACD request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's length profit with a 10% penalty surcharge for missing documentation; monthly default interest at 0.8%; where the undervaluation is wilful, penalty of up to 100% of the additional tax; protection of the tax base under the ATAD interest limitation rules (30% EBITDA cap) and reclassification of excessive debt as hidden profit distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executives signing false or incomplete TP documentation face personal criminal liability for tax fraud; directors can be held civilly liable for the shortfall where the TP adjustment renders the SCSp insolvent; departure bans and asset seizures may be ordered to secure the Treasury's claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/UBO register and beneficial ownership compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and register the ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp with the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) within one month of incorporation; use of bearer shares, trusts, or nominee arrangements to obscure ownership; acceptance of third-party funds for e-bike shipments without KYC verification; knowingly processing payments connected to sanctioned or politically exposed parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RBE registration violations: administrative fines of up to EUR 1,250,000 and, for repeated breaches, criminal fines; AML compliance failures under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 as amended: administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for serious breaches; criminal liability for money laundering with imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 1,250,000; freezing of bank accounts and transactions by the Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and any AML compliance officer are personally liable; criminal conviction triggers personal fines, debarment from management, travel bans, and imprisonment; asset freezes apply to personal assets where the funds are traceable to laundering; limited partners who interfere in the management of the partnership lose their limited liability protection and become exposed to the same sanctions.
